In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of effective systemic treatment for patients who have no clinical evidence of metastatic disease.
the treatment of patients with stage I breast cancer.
the identification and evaluation of effective adjuvant therapy for patients with early stage breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of adjuvant systemic therapy is beneficial in patients with stage I breast cancer.
oestrogen receptor status is a major determinant of the response of patients with stage I breast cancer to systemic adjuvant treatment.
the addition of systemic therapy to surgery for stage I breast cancer is beneficial in patients with oestrogen receptor negative tumours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results of the NSABP trials indicate that the treatment of node-negative patients with breast cancers that are oestrogen receptor positive or negative should be with tamoxifen or methotrexate plus 5-fluoro-uracil, respectively.
the addition of chemotherapy to surgery and the addition of tamoxifen to surgery are both beneficial in the treatment of breast cancer patients with positive oestrogen receptors.
oestrogen receptor status is an important prognostic factor in breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
systemic treatment is beneficial in patients with node-negative breast cancer.
adjuvant chemotherapy and endocrine treatment are effective in the management of early breast cancer.
adjuvant therapy is beneficial for both oestrogen receptor (ER) positive and ER negative patients with stage I breast cancer.
